hook: "A call ad variation that is crushing for us right now: customer service call ads" — 'crushing for us' + the novel variation.
cta: none explicit — the tactic is the deliverable.
idea: Instead of testimonial praise, record a real pre-purchase customer-service call: the customer asks the 5-6 questions buyers actually ask (pulled from the real support inbox), support answers one by one — removing objections instead of piling claims.
sequencing: The variation: real pre-purchase call, not testimonial.
The content: customer asks real buying questions, support answers.
The sourcing rule: pull questions from the real inbox + comments.
The psychology: every unanswered question is a lost purchase.
The mechanism: viewer hears their own doubt asked and answered.
formatting: Tactic-deep-dive: the variation named, the mechanics, the question-sourcing rule, the psychology. Photo attached.
why_it_works: Hearing your own doubt voiced by someone else is irresistible — it collapses the viewer's objection before the product page. Real-inbox sourcing guarantees the questions match the audience's actual stuck points.
what_to_steal: This is LC's 'DM I get every day' production method: pull the actual 5-6 top questions from LC's support inbox/comments ('will it tarnish? is it waterproof? will it turn my skin green?') and answer them as a call/DM conversation. 'Removes objections instead of piling claims' is the creative brief.
